evals.prompt: I just created a new TypeScript monorepo at github.com/acme-corp/platform. It has apps/web (Next.js), apps/admin (React), services/api (Fastify), and packages/ui and packages/utils. The repo has a docs/ folder with architecture.md and an ADRs/ directory. I want to set up GitHub as my project OS — labels, issue templates, PR template, a GitHub Project, all of it. Please analyze the repo structure and set up the full GitHub OS system for me.
evals.expected_output: Complete GitHub OS analysis and design: repository analysis (monorepo with 5 modules), label system (type, priority, area, module labels for web/admin/api/ui/utils), issue templates (task/bug/feature YAML), PR template, GitHub Project design, .github-os.json config, and a presentation for approval before execution.
assertions: Identifies the repo as a monorepo with 5 modules (web, admin, api, ui, utils)
Proposes module labels: module:web, module:admin, module:api, module:ui, module:utils
Proposes all four core type labels: type:feature, type:bug, type:chore, type:research
Proposes all four priority labels: priority:p0, priority:p1, priority:p2, priority:p3
Includes or proposes issue templates (task, bug, feature) as YAML forms
Includes or proposes a PR template with Closes #, What Changed, Context, Testing sections
Proposes creating a .github-os.json configuration file with module definitions
Presents the design for approval BEFORE executing (follows Step 3: Present Design)

evals.prompt: Hey, I have a single-repo project at github.com/zenji-dev/zen-piano (it's a virtual piano app). No docs folder yet, just a src/ directory and a README. I want to migrate from my current messy GitHub labels to the GitHub OS approach. Can you do a repo analysis and show me what you'd set up?
evals.expected_output: Repository analysis for a simple single repo with minimal docs. Skill detects: single repo, minimal docs (README only), proposes appropriate label set (no module labels needed or just one like module:zen-piano), proposes docs structure creation, and shows the analysis output format correctly.
assertions: Identifies the repo as a single repository (not monorepo)
Correctly assesses documentation as 'minimal' (README only, no docs/ directory)
Still proposes core type and priority labels even for a simple single repo
Suggests creating or setting up a docs/ directory as part of the recommendation
Produces a repo analysis report in the structured format defined by the skill
Does NOT generate unnecessary module labels for a simple single-repo project

evals.prompt: I need to write a GitHub issue for adding Stripe payment integration to our web app. Our repo is github.com/myco/saas-app. We already have the GitHub OS system set up (labels, templates, etc.). The feature will touch src/payments/, src/api/stripe.ts, and the frontend checkout flow. It needs to integrate with our existing subscription system and not break existing PayPal flow. Please write an LLM-ready issue following our GitHub OS standards.
evals.expected_output: A complete, LLM-ready GitHub issue body with: clear title, type:feature label recommendation, Context section with documentation links (docs/architecture.md#payments), Scope section (in/out of scope), Goal statement, Constraints, Acceptance Criteria checkboxes, and status:llm-ready label evaluation.
assertions: Issue has a clear, specific title under 72 characters (no vague title like 'Add payments')
Issue body contains a Context section with documentation and code links
Issue body contains an explicit Scope section with In Scope and Out of Scope items
Issue body contains Acceptance Criteria as a checklist ([ ] items)
Out of scope explicitly mentions PayPal (to not break existing flow)
Issue identifies specific files/paths to be affected (src/payments/, src/api/stripe.ts)
Evaluates or assigns status:llm-ready label based on the LLM-ready criteria checklist
